title: Class Planner
tagline: Helps City Tech students pick a career, then plan the classes to get there.
description: A quiz walks students toward a career path, then the planner maps the courses required to reach it — tracking prerequisites and what a student has already completed. The course catalog is scraped from City Tech's own site with a Python pipeline and transformed into the data the app reads.
highlights: Prerequisite resolution across a full degree catalog
Python scraper and transform pipeline feeding the front end

media.alt: Walking through the career quiz and into the course planner

title: Feed Picker
tagline: Recommends news articles to editors, turning ~12,000 scraped a day into a ranked shortlist.
description: Built at my internship, where editors were hand-picking every article out of about 12,000 scraped a day. An end-to-end machine learning system learns what the editors were already looking for and surfaces a ranked shortlist per section. A multi-stage filter first throws out low-quality scraped articles (missing images, wrong length, no category) before any expensive processing.
highlights: Cut the daily review pile from ~12,000 articles to a ranked shortlist of 8 per section
Filtering pipeline discards over 50% of raw input before any expensive processing

title: Pokédex: Elite Four Edition
tagline: A six-Pokémon team built to beat the Elite Four, as a browsable Pokédex.
description: Each team member shows up as a type-colored card; clicking one opens its full stat sheet and its role on the team. Built deliberately without a front-end framework — just HTML, CSS and JavaScript against an Express server reading from Postgres.
highlights: No front-end framework — routing and rendering by hand
Server-side routes with a real 404 page

media.alt: Browsing the team and opening a Pokémon's stat sheet

title: Barista App
tagline: Pick your drink by its properties and it finds the matching recipe.
description: A form collects what you want in a drink — temperature, milk, size — and the app matches it against a recipe set to return the right one. Small build, but it was the one that taught me how quickly a mismatched field name between a form and its JSON can quietly break everything downstream.
highlights: Component-to-component state passing across a multi-step form

media.alt: Filling out the drink form and getting a matched recipe
